items.title: Electric Cars To Cost The Same As Petrol Cars In 3 Years
points: For many car buyers, the argument against electric vehicles starts with the purchase price.
An EV may be cheaper to run, but the extra money paid at the showroom can be difficult to justify.
That gap could shrink sharply over the next few years.
The International Council on Clean Transportation (ICCT) expects most battery-electric cars to reach purchase-price parity with comparable petrol and diesel cars by around 2030.
Running an electric car can cost considerably less than fuelling a petrol car, especially when the owner has access to reasonably priced home charging.
If a comparable EV and petrol car cost roughly the same to buy, the lower running costs of the EV become an immediate advantage instead of a way to recover a large premium.
A prediction for the global market should not be read as a guarantee that every electric hatchback or SUV sold here will match its petrol equivalent by January 2030.

items.title: HistoriCity: Guru Padmasambhava and the Nyingma Tradition in Arunachal Pradesh

items.title: Hokchi lines up Mexican drilling campaign with Fontis jackup
points: Hokchi Energy, the Mexican subsidiary of Argentina’s Pan American Energy, has hired Fontis Energy’s Oberón jackup for a two-well exploration campaign in the shallow waters of the Gulf of Mexico.

The company is investing more than $60m to evaluate the Woolis and Tojol prospects offshore Veracruz, which have combined estimated prospective resources of around 100m barrels of oil equivalent and a geological success probability of 50%.
The 2013-built Oberón is already positioned off Coatzacoalcos, preparing to drill the Woolis-1EXP well during the third week of November.
Drilling is expected to continue into early 2027, with the second well scheduled immediately afterwards.
Both wells will target Lower Pliocene formations at depths of approximately 1,500 m.
The exploration programme forms part of a production-sharing contract signed in 2018, in which Hokchi holds a 75% stake and its affiliate Xaxamani Energy owns the remaining 25%.

Under the arrangement, SLB will provide integrated well delivery services for continuous exploration and development drilling campaigns.

The contract expands SLB’s existing relationship with Vår Energi, which already includes digital well and field development planning, as well as subsea production systems through its OneSubsea joint venture.
Vår Energi secured the Transocean Barents on a 1,095-day contract in April, worth approximately $490m in backlog.
